thread:
tess-support: Customer ACME (acct: acme-prod) reporting p99 latency jump ~400-600ms for text-generation endpoint starting ~13:02 UTC. Customer says behavior started after a burst. Can we triage? :eyes:
miro-oncall: Thanks — any request IDs or traces? If you have a sample request-id we can join traces across our egress logs.
sam-cs: Provided request-id 0x7a3f2c and a minimal curl we used: `curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer ***' -H 'X-Request-ID: 0x7a3f2c' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate`
aj-engineering: Pulling traces. Lina, can you check edge->egress hops for 0x7a3f2c? My quick glance at raw logs shows an unusual egress region: trace shows edge-us-west -> egress-eu-west1 -> edge-us-west -> model-host. That back-and-forth could explain the added RTT.
lina-telemetry: Pasted trace (trimmed):
```
trace_id: 0x7a3f2c
span 1: client -> edge-us-west (latency 20ms)
span 2: edge-us-west -> egress-eu-west1 (latency 210ms)
span 3: egress-eu-west1 -> edge-us-west (latency 200ms)
span 4: edge-us-west -> model-host-us-west (latency 40ms)
```

lina-telemetry: Route metadata: routing_policy: region_affinity=preferred, fallback=auto, pool_id=edge-us-west-pool-42, egress_gateway=egress-eu-west1 (selected by egress-selector rule due to available capacity flag).

tess-support: Customer is surprised, they didn't change settings. They upgraded traffic but expected local serving.

aj-engineering: Hypothesis: when local serving pool hit a soft cap the smart router selected an egress gateway in eu-west1 because that gateway reported spare capacity and was marked compatible with model variant. But selected gateway caused cross-region detour instead of local fallback. We should check the selector scoring.

miro-oncall: I queried routing decisions around that time. Score dump for pool-42:
```
pool-42 scores:
  edge-us-west: score 0.62 (util 0.98)
  edge-us-east: score 0.40 (util 0.55)
  egress-eu-west1: score 0.81 (util 0.30) <-- chosen due to scoring heuristic (prefers lower util even if region mismatch)
```

aj-engineering: That's the bug path: scoring didn't enforce region_affinity hard constraint when fallback=auto. It favored lower-util egress even across region. We need to change selector to prefer same-region gateways unless explicitly marked global.

lina-telemetry: Added trace link to internal dashboard: https://telemetry.redwood.ai/trace/0x7a3f2c (internal) and exported sample pcap for network team.

deploy-bot: Canary rollback note: canary routing rule `egress-selector-v2` was deployed 3 minutes before the spike (deploy id d-9876). Rolling back now to v1 as mitigation.

miro-oncall: Mitigation checklist: 1) rollback egress-selector-v2 (in progress), 2) patch scoring to respect region_affinity for fallback=auto (PR created by @aj-engineering), 3) customer workaround: pin region via `region=us-west` parameter or use dedicated pool, 4) follow-up postmortem and alerting on cross-region detours.

sam-cs: Communicated to ACME: we rolled back a recent routing change and have a patch queued; advised temporary `region=us-west` pin. Customer happy with workaround for now.

tess-support: ACME confirmed latency back to baseline after rollback, p99 down to ~65ms. Please keep me posted on PR and postmortem timeline. :thumbsup:

aj-engineering: PR link: https://git.internal/r/redwood/infra/pulls/2345 — addresses selector heuristic + adds unit tests for region affinity. Target deploy in next maintenance window; if you need faster we can hotfix the scoring function.

miro-oncall: I'll run a synthetic test job to simulate load and ensure we don't regress. Plan to close incident once 24h stable.

lina-telemetry: Adding an alert rule: if trace shows >1 cross-region detour per 10k requests in a 5m window, fire pager.

tess-support: Great, thanks everyone. Closing loop with ACME now and filing follow-up.

sam-cs: ACME left a note: "Thanks — visibility and quick response helped a lot" :heart:
